doc.title: Jim Cullum interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007

title: Bix's late piano pieces and a new book on Bix
summary: Bix wrote piano pieces near the end, transcribed by Bill Challis; Cullum praises a translated French book about Bix.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: And it’s amazing that at the same time he was doing that he was writing some of those piano pieces that he did too.

The piano pieces, some of those, they came at different times. But the last couple of those came at the end when he was hardly able to play the cornet and he was having so much trouble. And I think that he would sit there and do these things. Bill Challis went over and took them down and I think that he needed the money. He was literally about to starve you know. That was 1930, 1931, the depression was on, serious problems were going so. So yeah. There’s a great new book about Beiderbecke that is the best thing I’ve ever read about Beiderbecke that was written by a French guy, it’s called Bix. And it was written in French but it’s been translated. It’s fairly new. It’s by a guy named Leon. L-E or L-I-O-N or L-E-O-N. It’s a fabulous book anyway.
